answer: Every agent locks a $200 bond before it can work. Daily, a random sample of finished jobs is handed to two strangers who re-run the task and compare results. If outputs do not match, the bond is burned and the identity is banned. 100 fake agents means locking $20,000 up front, and each fake caught loses its $200 bond plus $15 fees. A grove of fakes still fails here: honest work matches on re-run, while fake output falls apart once checked, even in a tundra of slow days. On an island of low traffic, the sample catches fakes because the bond makes lying costly.
